I do really like this game, but it desperately needs some balancing adjustments, especially early-game in the first few maps and in single-player mode. As it currently exists, I have a very love-but-mostly-hate relationship with it. 
 
The game is fine in multiplayer mode. It's silly, it's fun with your friends, and its mechanics aren't difficult to pick up and learn. However, it is JUST fine. The monsters need to be balanced much better than they are, ESPECIALLY some of the tier 3 monsters and ESPECIALLY for the first 1~4 levels of the game. You shouldn't be contending with a tier 3 headman monster in the first or second map of a new game when you've still got no tools, weapons, or meaningful upgrades to help you deal with it. Tier 3 monsters should not be spawning in the first couple levels of the game at all in their current state when they can be so abysmally difficult to deal with. 
 
If the devs don't want to touch any of that, then there should at least be vanilla tools that let you customize the game spawns or overall difficulty to your preference. It's not fun playing in a group of 5 where the same 1-2 players are the only ones left alive on every level because your more casual or weaker or simply misfortunate friends continuously just get totally annihilated by the floating head or a clown. I do like REPO, but there are so many frustrating things in this game that have ruined me enjoying this game as much as I'd want to enjoy it. There IS a good game here, but I don't see many people pointing out the MANY negative or frustrating aspects of this game, so I wanted to point some of these out and I hope the developers see this so the game can be the best that it can be.

Firstly let me talk about maybe my biggest issue, the Huntsman AI. I don't know why many people think he is ok, but I've heard it's worse on the host's end and I host often so maybe that's why I have such an Issue with it and others don't. I have had MANY times where he shoots me either across an entire room where I could not hope to react and get one tapped, or he shoots me when ANOTHER sound source made him trigger and he shoots me anyway. I've had times where I tap a object on the ground to bait his shot, and instead of shooting the object far away from me he shoots me instead. This makes absolutely no sense and I personally think he should not work this way, he should always shoot the sound source not the nearest player like how he does at times. I suggest taking inspiration from the Eyeless Dogs from Lethal Company, just make him not instantly shoot at the first sound he hears and make him have an audio cue where players can be aware they are making too much noise like a sound of him grumbling or him going "huh", and if they continue he then shoots them. I also think his idle sounds should play

I don't know what's changed but now it just seems more difficult than fun. It's fun to die every now and again,  but this seems just unfun now.  
 
Add a difficulty slider already
It’s a really fun and amusing game to play with friends. However, lately, matches have been closing on their own due to server timeout issues. This makes it unplayable; hopefully, they fix it soon.

While this game can be quite fun and hilarious with friends, I simply cannot recommend it for how unfair it is. Very few deaths in this game feels like your own fault as most of the time, you simply got unlucky or some random bs just one shots you. These issues are even worse when playing solo. One bad situation forces you to start all over again.

After trying out the new update, it is safe to say that none of the issues have been addressed. Several months of waiting, and the only major changes to the game are cosmetic, both for the player and the environment/maps. It also does not help that the player cosmetics are obtained through lootboxes, where there is a possibility of only obtaining a singular sock (not a pair) and a singular sleeve (again, not a pair). One of the few notable inclusion gameplay-wise is the new Defibro item, which revives a player. Yes, it does give solo players a second chance, however, it is not only very rare to find, it is also extremely expensive for a one-time use revive. This means that even getting your hands on one is purely luck, let alone actually affording it early on. Another is the newly added vehicles are also pretty bad for solo play, as trying to loot with them is annoying, even when riding the Hauler as it can't hold even medium-sized objects.

I'm really disappointed to see where the devs have taken this game. As someone who has been playing the game for almost a year and has about 113 Hours, the game seems to make a steep decline with each update. This game had so much potential to be an enjoyable and replayable game but with the October 2025 update- it seems absolutely unredeemable.  
Instead of finding new and interesting ways to raise the difficulty in the game, the devs have added a bunch of random new monsters who range from childishly easy to 'rip your hair out' difficulties. The two main monsters I hold issue with are the green ghost (who moves to fast to shoot and I've yet to kill) and the bug (who once touches you, prevents you from defending yourself in any capacity and leads to a quick gameover).  
Not to mention now instead of having a few monsters spawning every thirty seconds or so now there are four spawning in the same room as you.  
The other glaring issue with this game is it's godawful RNG and shop spawns. With a bad string of luck that has you replaying level 1 ten times before making it to level 2, it doesn't exactly feel fair. The highest level I was able to reach in the newest update was 11 but it was completely unenjoyable. While you could laugh and mess around with friends before, there is absolutely no margin for error now.  
It seems the devs focus completely on the social media and community aspect of the game forgetting the most important part of that... being the game. Adding a dozen

That in combination with things like the eye monster popping up mid jump in pit rooms (its so frequent that vents in McJacknet is becoming nearly unusable). Fighting enemies after round 3 or 4 was what made repo feel unique from all the other (dont die from the thing) horror games and moving away from that has just made the game feel slow and less satifying.

The game feels unplayable without weapons. Early rounds are difficult in an annoying way because you have  to constantly hide and hope your items do not get destroyed by monster that you cannot fight against without good weapons. Most hiding places also seem to be broken and monsters can find you easily. Early stages are just too annoying to want to play through at this point. Having weapons show up random in the shop was ok when you could more easily hide or avoid monsters, but now the difficulty without anyway to defend yourself just feels punishing.

This game was pretty perfect before the monsters update. Endlessly replayable in multiplayer, and great in single player too. The monsters update has ruined the game for me. Single player is unplayable now, even for my save game with 600 health and 15-20 of every upgrade. It's just too hard. Multiplayer isn't quite so bad, but some monsters are OP beyond reason, and sometimes there is just no way to win regardless of how good you are. The new death behaviour looked like it would be really fun and useful, but in practice... you can barely move at all, can't see the map, and your voice sounds muffled and broken to the point your friends can't understand you. 
 
Hopefully the devs fix this, because now I don't recommend new players buy the game.

There's a good core game here, but unfortunately it's not built for solo gamers at all. It very much requires you to have a multiplayer group. Which if you don't have any gaming friends and you don't like randoms, means you're out of luck. The fact that the game deletes your saves when you die is also a horrible mechanic intended to create false difficulty. The monsters are not balanced for single player, the maps at a certain stage become almost unplayable due to the amount of random death pits that spawn alongside the monsters, and even if you somehow clear a map, the game will typically spawn or teleport every monster in the map to the extraction point and then they just sit there and spawn camp it, making it impossible to win.  
 
It's a shame because when the game is working well, the collection mechanic is really fun and addicting. There's just unfortunately all the other bad stuff that is built around it. Fans of this game will defend it by saying 'well its early access', but...Game has been out for a long time and the developer isn't adding anything actually needed by the game, just for fun, silly stuff. 
 
Most of the stuff the game needs are done by player mods, which is not acceptable. 
 
Overall, really fun core mechanics and gameplay that is addicting, but there's just too much other unfair stuff built into the game to make it a must have. Especially for solo gamers.

This game isn't about stealth. It's about hiding in a corner for frustrating amounts of time while slow creatures lumber around right where you need to be. It's a game about enemies getting cheep shots in before you know they are there. It's a game about tantalizingly damageable enemies that kill you far to easily if you don't swing your mouse just right when you go to hit them. It's a game that punishes you when you try to do anything other than hide. In short, everything about this game is frustrating for me to the extreme. What's worse, is according to my friend group, it's a good game, and I am fun to play with. So, I'm still playing the master class of a rage gripping slog of a game, ripping my hair out and begging for them to find another game to play. I can't really say it's a bad game, but I can say it is not for me.

This game feels like something that was thrown together at a hackathon without much consideration given to...well anything. If I had to sum up this game with a word, it would be "unforgiving". The tutorial explains the basic movement controls and not much else. Everything else you learn about the game will be through trial and error, which often results in destroyed valuables or your death. The shop items are not explained. How to recharge weapons is not explained. The fact that you can even KILL ENEMIES is not explained. The first level spawns enemies that one shot you, sometimes from across the room (huntsman). Unless you're drunk or farming clips for youtube shorts, this game will get old quickly.

I wanted to like the game, but it actively screws you over just for the sake of screwing you over. It seemed like a challenge, but in the end you can do everything right and still lose the level depending on how and when monsters spawn. With that aspect and the fact you have to start back at level 1 every time just creates a loop of frustration and resentment to the game. Which they already have my money so.... good for them I guess? 
 
This game is not solo friendly at all. Its only redeeming quality seems to be the click bait clips and the moments of "oh did you see that?"

I gave this game a go a few times. I want to love it so much because the basic idea is just great. With a group of close friends it makes so much fun to sneak around, steal stuff and try to avoid the enemies. But that's where the problem is: the enemies. They all seem to have some sort of aim bot included. Meet them once in an unfortunate situation: dead. Because a blind man obiously never misses with his shotgun. Try to get back to extraction: you can't. Enemy keeps patrolling constantly on the only exit route. That's pure frustration. I'd also reconsider the respawning option: why not just have your friends respawn when you find them. Sitting there watching others struggle is also no fun. This is a game. Let us play not watch. I for once will wait and see if this gets some balancing tweaks that make the game the fun group game that I'd want it to be. If not, then maybe it's just not for me.

This game is loads of nonsense fun with a group of friends! ...If you have a fantastic internet connection. If you have a sub-par internet connection, be prepared to get constantly kicked due to client timeouts. Of all the games I play online with friends, this one in particular REFUSES to allow me to actually play online with others. It is absolutely the most unforgiving of less-than-perfect internet connections, and it is BEYOND frustrating as someone who genuinely wants to enjoy this game! I don't have this issue this bad with any other games. There is no reason it should be this bad. And for some reason, the developers simply aren't fixing it. For those of us who don't have any access to better options, it's a slap in the face, and quite frankly ruins any enjoyment I could've otherwise had. For that reason alone, I'm not recommending this, and honestly wish I could've gotten my money back.

One of the best games, ruined by one of the worst multiplayer system. It's an online game (photon servers), you cannot play it without Ethernet connection in LAN. Even if you have 2 PC connected in one local network, player who connected to your lobby will have ugly ass ping, in physic based game! Host doesn't have any struggels, but you can't rely on your crewmates, especially giving them weapons and grenades. This game is a waste of money, and one of the funniest games at the same time, and only because it doesn't have a LAN or Peer to Peer multiplayer. By the way Lethal Company doesn't have this kind of problems, and you can play it in LAN and it's a peer to peer connection game, so you can blame only your or your friend ethernet connection.
One of the biggest regrets of all times, because it's not fun to see how your friends can't even pick up a damn thing without breaking it, they can't even tumble jump without problems. But it's an amazing game, so hope devolepers will change that problems and will add a LAN connection and peer to peer connection.

I'm at a point now where I'm honestly unsure of whether I can recommend this game. It is fun for a while, and maybe for the money it's still worth it, but the monsters update was the last major update that really changed the core gameplay loop of REPO. And it came out October 30th 2025, almost a year ago as of writing this review. The cosmetics update added a bit but nothing that would substantially lengthen the games lifespan. If the game felt dry and boring before the cosmetic update, the cosmetic update maybe gave the game another week or two of life before you just found it kinda boring again. And I'll be honest, part of that isn't the dev's fault but is the fault of the public community.

If you want longevity out of this game, public lobbies are where you need to go. But it's infuriating now, you'll find most lobbies are late join which crashes your game if you join them in the loading screen - all you'll be able to do is HEAR other semibots while looking at a frozen loading screen. You can't talk to them yourself, you can just hear the sounds of other people having fun. You have to Alt + F4 and relaunch just to fix this. Then find another lobby! I'd say a good 75% of lobbies at least will end like that. At least.

The other 25% is going to be made up of some percentage of Russians, Children, lobbies with mods that make the game unfun (infinite health, noclip, spawning weapons, "free cosmetics :D", etc.), some combination of those options, and every now and again you'll

I like R.E.P.O. with friends, but if you're a solo player, it gets almost unbeatable around level 3. for example The tick attaches to you and starts draining your health. The only way to survive is by getting health upgrades or having a teammate remove the tick in the games I've played . I've gotten past level 3 solo, but it just gets too hard for me.
With teammates, it's a fun game. You can tell it's made for multiplayer, and it's a much more enjoyable experience with friends. So, for solo runs, it's a 4/10 for me—but for multiplayer, it's a solid 9.5/10

R.E.P.O. is one of those projects that seems to get more praise than it really earns. The concept might sound intriguing at first, but the execution feels messy and overhyped. The tone jumps around without focus, and instead of leaving a strong impression, it just drags on. I can see why some people admire its style, but for me, it doesn’t deserve all the attention it gets. It tries to be bold and clever, yet ends up feeling forced and inconsistent. Overall, it’s more exhausting than engaging.
